claims.text: The investigated HEA has an equimolar WTaTiVZr composition.
The HEA and commercial pure tungsten can be compared with similar grain sizes and controlled grain-boundary structures.
The WTaTiVZr HEA exhibits severe lattice distortion.
Chemical disorder in the WTaTiVZr HEA produces local fluctuations in stacking-fault energy.
The HEA has a random atomic distribution.
Severe lattice distortion lowers the effective Peierls barrier and other activation barriers for dislocation motion.
Local fluctuations in stacking-fault energy enable activation of multiple slip systems.
The combined lattice-distortion and stacking-fault-energy effects enable dynamic dislocation recovery during high-temperature deformation.
The proposed dislocation mechanisms produce a more homogeneous stress distribution than in pure tungsten.
Activation of multiple slip systems facilitates more homogeneous plastic deformation.
The proposed mechanism improves WTaTiVZr toughness relative to commercial pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
The HEA will have a lower creep strain rate than pure tungsten under the controlled high-temperature comparison.
The HEA will develop a more uniform dislocation network than pure tungsten.
Several slip systems will operate simultaneously in the HEA relative to pure tungsten.
The HEA will exhibit lower nanoindentation-derived yield stress than pure tungsten.
The HEA will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten.
Crack initiation will be delayed in the HEA relative to pure tungsten.
The hypothesis is applicable from 800 to 1200 °C in inert atmospheres when grain size is carefully controlled.
Outside the specified temperature, atmosphere, or grain-size conditions, alternative deformation mechanisms may operate.
Matched high-temperature tests and atomistic simulations can assess dislocation behavior, slip activation, yield behavior, creep, and local stacking-fault-energy landscapes in the two materials.
